title: Inflation
examples: Teacher, if prices go up, does my money buy less stuff?
What is the difference between inflation and a price increase?
How can I tell if inflation is bad for me?

explain.say: Today we will learn about inflation and how it affects money.

items: Prices for goods go up over time.
Your money buys less than before.

explain.say: Inflation means that the general price level of goods rises.
When inflation rises, the value of your savings decreases.
We measure inflation using a basket of goods approach.
For example, if bread costs two dollars last year, and now costs three dollars, that is inflation.
In real life, think about a favorite snack you buy every week.

faq.q: Does inflation mean that all prices go up?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but it means that the average price level is rising. It suggests that the cost of living is generally increasing.
asks: Does inflation mean everything is more expensive?

faq.q: If I keep my money under the mattress, does inflation affect it?
faq.a: Yes, keeping cash at home loses value over time due to inflation. The money you save buys less stuff later on.
asks: Does my savings lose value at home?

faq.q: What is the Consumer Price Index, or CPI?
faq.a: The CPI tracks the average change in prices paid by urban consumers for a basket of goods. It is a key measure of inflation.
asks: What is the CPI used for?

faq.q: Is a small price increase always inflation?
faq.a: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level, not just one item. A single item going up might be due to supply issues.
asks: Is one high price the same as inflation?
When is a price rise just a normal change?

faq.q: Does inflation mean the economy is doing badly?
faq.a: High or unpredictable inflation can signal economic problems. However, some managed inflation is normal for a growing economy.
asks: Is inflation always bad for the economy?
What is a good rate of inflation?

facts: Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises.
It means that your money buys less than it did before.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a common way to measure inflation.
Savings kept in cash lose purchasing power due to inflation.

quiz.say: If a loaf of bread cost one dollar last year and costs one dollar twenty-five cents this year, what is the approximate rate of inflation?
quiz.why: You calculate the percentage increase by dividing the new price by the old price, then subtracting one.

wrong.0: You might forget to write the percent sign, making it seem like a simple number.
wrong.1: This is the correct decimal, but the question asks for the percentage rate.
wrong.2: You might just state the new price instead of calculating the change.

quiz.say: Which concept describes what happens to the amount of goods you can buy with a fixed amount of money?
quiz.why: Inflation causes your purchasing power to decrease because prices are higher.

wrong.0: While prices fluctuate, inflation describes a general, sustained trend.
wrong.2: This would mean your money can buy more things, which is the opposite of inflation.
wrong.3: This would mean there is no change in the cost of living at all.

quiz.say: If the CPI rose from 100 to 110 over a year, what does this suggest about the cost of living?

options.show: Prices increased by one hundred ten percent
options.say: Prices increased by one hundred ten percent

quiz.why: A rise from 100 to 110 means a 10 percent increase in the average cost of goods.

wrong.1: This would mean the cost of living got cheaper, which is deflation.
wrong.2: This would mean the CPI remained at 100, showing no change.
wrong.3: You might multiply the numbers instead of finding the percentage change.
